**Not in this slice:** `catalog cite` and `catalog uncite`, the slice Cites line, the retired assumption or decision callout on a roadmap row, agent instructions, and the README command row. `fields.cites` is stored so the index schema bumps once; nothing writes it yet.

## Why

A prose blob cannot be cited, retired, or reordered one statement at a time. Records give each statement a stable id and a lifecycle without putting planning rows on `slicer next`.

## Implement

Index schema is 8. A missing `catalog` object and a missing `fields.cites` load empty and do not write. The next index save stamps 8.

`catalog` stores `next_id`, `id_prefix` `C`, `id_width` 2, and `records`. A record is `id`, `kind`, `title`, `body`, `status`, `reason`, `successor`. Kinds are `goal`, `non_goal`, `requirement`, `constraint`, `decision`, `assumption`. Status is `active` or `retired`.

```
slicer catalog add --kind goal "Title" --body "text"
slicer catalog list --kind non-goal --retired
slicer catalog show C01
slicer catalog edit C01 --title "Title" --body "text"
slicer catalog retire C01 --reason "why" --successor C02
slicer catalog move C03 --before C01
```

`--kind` accepts `non-goal` and stores `non_goal`. `list` shows active records in editorial order; `--retired` appends retired ones. `move` stays inside one kind and preserves the relative order of other kinds. Retire requires a nonempty reason, may name one same-kind successor, and freezes the record. A successor cycle, a different kind, or an unknown id is refused before writing. Retired records are not purged and their ids are not reused.

`slicer goals` keeps `goals` and `non_goals` and adds active goal and non-goal records. `--retired` includes retired ones. With no records, its text stays as it is now.

Empty records leave `ROADMAP.md` and `ROADMAP.html` byte-identical, so the render format stays 1. Goal and non-goal records render under the existing headings, prose first. The other four kinds render from `{{catalog}}`, one heading per nonempty kind, active records then retired. History uses action `catalog` with note `add`, `edit`, `retire`, or `move`.

`check` fails when a successor names nothing, the successor's kind differs, a successor cycle exists, a retired record has a blank reason, an active record has a reason, a catalog id collides with an item id, or `catalog.next_id` would reuse an id. The new error code is `no_such_record`.

Allocation uses the catalog counter and floors it from sibling worktrees the way item ids do. `list`, `next`, `stats`, and `deps` ignore records.
